A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ARTEMIS study. All 29 pages, including figures, tables, equations, references, and Appendices A–K, support reliable comparison. The appendices are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: V1 reports original penetration-testing results from ten professionals and AI agents, Cybench evaluations, and vulnerability elicitation trials in Tables 1–3. Appendix B documents individual findings.

after.justification: V2 retains the original live-network comparisons, Cybench evaluations, elicitation trials, and detailed appendix findings. These remain original empirical results despite being retained from v1.

M1.justification: The supervisor, dynamically prompted sub-agents, session management, and vulnerability triage procedure remain unchanged in Section 3.3 and Appendix A. The new refusal interpretation does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same university network, ten professionals, Cybench tasks, and four vulnerability elicitation targets. The expanded ethics description does not establish new task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the live-network and Cybench experiments. V1 already explains that all non-ARTEMIS Cybench results use CyAgent; v2 makes these existing scaffold/model pairings explicit in Table 2.

E3.justification: Both versions retain 16-hour ARTEMIS execution, scoring of the first 10 hours, the same model configurations, and the same elicitation protocol. Table 2 newly discloses CyAgent GPT-5 pass@1 evaluation, without establishing a changed metric or rerun.

E4.justification: The five-level hint experiment in Section 5.3/Table 3, behavioral and cost analyses, Appendix E case study, and Appendix H vulnerability-overlap analysis are unchanged. No new ablation or robustness experiment supports the added refusal interpretation.

E5.justification: No repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added. Table 2's new statement of no significant scaffold uplift repeats the existing sampling-variance interpretation; the limitation concerning insufficient statistical power is retained.

E6.justification: Section 8 newly reports remediation of all identified vulnerabilities before publication and no observed unsafe or out-of-scope activity from any participant, extending v1's narrower agent-scope observation. Performance values, rankings, costs, and appendix findings are unchanged, including Table 2's 48.6% ARTEMIS and 45.9% CyAgent GPT-5 success rates.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions and Equations 1–3, together with Appendix K's complexity framework, are unchanged. Neither version adds mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: a live-enterprise human–agent comparison, the ARTEMIS scaffold, strong relative performance and cost advantages, and remaining capability gaps.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly attributes ARTEMIS's lack of refusals, compared with Claude Code and MAPTA using corresponding underlying models, to scaffolding and prompting bypassing refusal mechanisms. This adds a causal interpretation to existing observations. The main limitations and Cybench interpretation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 2 specifies the authors' CyAgent GPT-5 pass@1 evaluation and its leaderboard provenance. Section 8 adds operational safety definitions, monitor qualifications and training, and three termination mechanisms. Conversely, Sections 4.2/5.4 omit the previous 9am–5pm, two-day scheduling detail. These are documentation changes rather than demonstrated procedural changes.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and novelty positioning are unchanged. Table 2 clarifies existing comparison identities without introducing a new prior-work relationship.

P1.justification: Localized edits expand the ethics statement, add the refusal explanation, streamline execution-time and cost wording, and correct an acknowledgement name. Section order and the broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 changes from two columns to separate Scaffold, Model, and Success columns, with an expanded caption. This shifts the adjacent Figure 2 and surrounding text slightly. Other displays and all appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves transparency through clearer scaffold/model attribution and evaluation provenance in Table 2, plus concrete monitoring and remediation disclosures in Section 8. These gains improve auditability without strengthening the main performance evidence. The loss of exact daily scheduling detail and the stronger refusal attribution without new controlled evidence temper the improvement.
